tenant_id.description: Workspace to act in, for a session (the X-Tenant-ID header does the same and wins when both are sent). Ignored for API keys, which stay in their own workspace. A malformed value is answered 400; a workspace the user is not a member of, 403; no workspace at all on a workspace-scoped operation, 401.
tenant_id.name: tenant_id

BadRequest.description: Malformed tenant_id or X-Tenant-ID (error bad_request), or a request the handler rejected (validation_error).

Error.description: Any other error: 404 not_found, 409 on a conflicting change, 500 internal_error, 503 when a dependency (NATS, local AI) is unavailable, and others. Most answers use the JSON envelope; a few low-level paths answer plain text.

Forbidden.description: The credential may not do this: a viewer or read-scope API key on a write, a workspace the user is not a member of, or an operation that needs a tenant admin or superadmin session.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited (API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, per credential, or per address for anonymous calls and failed authentication). error is rate_limited; wait Retry-After seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a request is accepted again.

Unauthorized.description: No valid credential (missing, expired or revoked session or API key), or a workspace-scoped operation called without a workspace.

config.description: Secret fields, by monitor type, are listed in x-probara-secret-fields; they are encrypted at rest and read back as "***".

apiKey.description: Workspace API key with read or write scope, bound to the workspace that created it. API keys cannot call operations that need a tenant admin or superadmin session. MCP OAuth access tokens are refused here: they are valid only on the MCP endpoint.

session.description: Operator session cookie, set by the operator UI's sign-in. Select the workspace with the tenant_id query parameter or the X-Tenant-ID header. Roles come from the user's workspace membership.
session.name: admin_access

info.description:
Probara's REST API, generated from the same catalog as the MCP tools and checked against the router, so every operation listed here is routed. Routes deliberately left out are listed with the reason under x-probara-not-described; health and metrics endpoints (/healthz, /readyz, /metrics) live outside /api/v1 and are not described.

Authenticate with a workspace API key (Authorization: Bearer pk_…) or an operator session cookie. A session picks the workspace of a workspace-scoped operation with the tenant_id query parameter (or the X-Tenant-ID header); an API key is bound to its workspace and ignores both.

Response bodies are described only where the handler's Go response type is known; other operations say so. Errors usually use the JSON envelope {"error": code, "message": text}, but a few low-level paths answer plain text, so branch on the status code first. List endpoints take 1-based page and page_size; a page_size above the maximum is lowered to it, and a missing or invalid value takes the default.
info.title: Probara API

get.description: One alert channel's notification attempts, test sends included, newest first, with each alert's kind and monitor name (or location names for offline-location and mesh alerts). Use it to see why a channel stopped delivering; get_alert_channel carries the failing flag (a failure in the last 24 hours with no success since). Each row has event_type (created, reminder, resolved, acknowledged, suspected_cause), attempt, path (sync: sent by the alerter; async: queued, then sent by a delivery worker), test (a channel test send), recipient (masked; one row per recipient on SMS), outcome and reason, a sanitized error, provider_status and duration_ms. Outcomes: delivered; failed (transient, retried; reason retries_exhausted on the worker's last attempt, plugin_missing when the worker build lacks the channel type); permanent_failure (not retried; reason egress_blocked when the notification egress policy refused the address, invalid_config); dropped (a queued event deliberately not sent: reason resolved = the alert resolved first, unacknowledged = an acknowledgement notice after an unacknowledge, muted = held by an acknowledgement or snooze and not sent again, muted_requeued = a held page that reached nobody, sent once the mute lifts, reopened = a recovery notice dropped because the alert relapsed and is open again, earlier_episode = queued before the alert relapsed, channel_inactive, channel_changed). event_type relapsed is a relapse notice (sent to the channel as a page). Drops are not failures.

post.description:
Invite a user to set up their account. method "password" issues a single-use set-your-password link valid 7 days for an account that has no password yet (a newer invite replaces it); the account then has a Probara password and is never linked to the SSO identity provider by email, so it signs in without the provider's MFA. method "sso" tells the user to sign in with single sign-on. With single sign-on enabled, method is required unless the account is already linked (then "sso"); without SSO it defaults to "password". The link is emailed to the account; without email delivery or an address, the response's link is the one copy to hand over (delivered=false, reason says why). Superadmins only.

Access: Needs a superadmin session; API keys are refused. Needs write access: viewers and read-scope API keys get 403.

400.description: Invalid method; or single sign-on is enabled and no method was given for an account not linked to the identity provider yet (validation_error).

409.description: The account is disabled, signs in with single sign-on (password invite), already has a password, or single sign-on is not configured (sso invite).

502.description: Email delivery is configured but the mail could not be sent (delivery_failed); the link is not returned.

post.description:
Issue a single-use password reset link (valid 1 hour; a newer one replaces it) for a password account. Emailed to the account when email delivery is configured; otherwise the response's link is the one copy to hand over. Completing the reset signs the user out of every browser session and revokes their MCP connections (workspace API keys are not the user's and stay). Not for SSO accounts or accounts without a password (invite_user). Superadmins only.

Access: Needs a superadmin session; API keys are refused. Needs write access: viewers and read-scope API keys get 403.
